title: Status buildup
subtitle: Accumulate pressure first, apply the consequence only at the threshold
summary: Boss attacks fill a separate status gauge; the actual effect begins only when accumulated exposure reaches its threshold.
overview: Status buildup separates exposure from consequence. Each qualifying contact adds to a readable gauge, safe time may let that value decay, and the authored effect is applied exactly once when the threshold is crossed, creating a risk decision before ordinary damage, control loss, or defeat occurs.
learning: Define which contacts add buildup, the per-source amount, threshold, decay delay and rate, effect payload and duration, cleansing rules, resistance scaling, reapplication immunity, stacking ownership, UI priority, and the tests that keep buildup, effect, and ordinary health damage from becoming one ambiguous system.

demo.title: Enter Kern's rune field, let one exposure decay, then cross the threshold
phaseNames: Apply partial buildup, then show delayed decay
Stack contacts to the threshold and apply one effect
Clear the gauge, protect re-entry, and reset
phaseDescriptions: Tavi enters Kern's radial field and receives 38 buildup at 0.72 s. Leaving the field stops new exposure, but the gauge holds until its 1.08 s decay delay and then falls to 14 by 1.72 s, making the grace period and recovery rate separately visible.

Tavi re-enters before the remainder clears. Contacts at 2.14 s and 2.60 s raise the same gauge to 55 and then 100. The threshold crossing reserves one status effect; the rune lock begins at 2.72 s and lasts until 3.72 s while ordinary health remains a separate concern.

When the effect ends, buildup resets to zero and a solid shield marks immunity until 4.42 s. A contact while the shield is present is ignored rather than starting another effect. Tavi then leaves the field and the system returns to its clear state after 5.20 s.
demo.danger: The radial field adds buildup only during authored contact windows; partial exposure is not yet the status effect, and crossing the threshold may never create more than one effect event
demo.locked: Source id, buildup amount, threshold comparison, decay delay, decay rate, resistance modifier, effect id, duration, cleansing, immunity, and reapplication authority are encounter-owned
demo.safe: Show current buildup, threshold, decay direction, active effect, cleanse, and immunity as distinct shapes and states; never communicate all of them with one changing color
demo.reducedMotion: Autoplay is disabled by reduced motion. Scrub across 0.72, 1.08, 1.72, 2.14, 2.60, 2.72, 3.72, 4.42, and 5.20 seconds to inspect exposure, decay, threshold, effect, immunity, and reset.
demo.diagramDescription: Four rune stones anchor Kern’s filled exposure field while Tavi enters and leaves it. The solid gauge above the arena rises after contact, partly decays away from the field, then reaches its threshold on two further contacts. Stone shackles appear beside Tavi for one status effect. When the gauge clears, a solid shield beside Tavi marks brief immunity and blocks another contact.

steps.title: What accumulates, and what does not happen before the threshold?
steps.body: Give every source a stable status id and explicit buildup amount. Decide whether blocks, invulnerability, shields, weak hits, overlapping zones, or repeated ticks contribute. Keep partial buildup free of the final payload unless a separate escalating-warning rule is intentional; otherwise the gauge lies about when the consequence begins.

steps.title: How can the player manage the gauge before it fills?
steps.body: Tune the delay before decay, decay per second, cleansing cost, resistance modifier, and safe-space availability together. Test one isolated contact, a planned combo, overlapping sources, and the slowest legal movement speed. The player needs enough signal to decide whether to leave, cleanse, guard, or accept the risk.

steps.title: What exactly happens on crossing, clearing, and reapplication?
steps.body: Use one authoritative threshold comparison and reserve one effect id when it crosses. Specify whether excess buildup is discarded, carried, or converted; when the gauge clears; whether the effect can refresh; and how long immunity lasts. Test simultaneous final hits, cleanse-on-crossing, phase changes, death, rollback, and repeated network messages.

mistakes.title: The gauge looks full before the effect is authoritative
mistakes.body: Rounding, delayed replication, or a decorative animation can show 100 while the server still considers the target below threshold. Derive fill, threshold flash, effect event, and accessibility announcement from the same resolved value and sequence number.

mistakes.title: Decay and immunity are invisible exceptions
mistakes.body: If buildup pauses, falls, clears, or ignores a new hit without a distinct cue, the system appears inconsistent. Expose delay, direction, cleansing, resistance, and immunity separately, and log the reason every contribution was applied, reduced, or rejected.

designNotes.title: Separate buildup from the applied effect
designNotes.body: Store current buildup, last exposure time, threshold, effect state, effect timer, and immunity timer as separate fields. The gauge may decay while no effect exists; the active effect may continue while buildup is already zero. This boundary prevents accidental refreshes and supports clear telemetry.

designNotes.title: Balance frequency, amount, and recovery as one rhythm
designNotes.body: A small amount from a rapid source can be more demanding than one large, slow pulse because it repeatedly postpones decay. Measure time to threshold under intended and worst-case overlap, time needed to recover after one mistake, safe uptime lost, and how resistance changes those values.

designNotes.title: Choose an effect proportional to avoidability
designNotes.body: A hard stun or instant defeat needs stronger advance information, more reliable counterplay, and safer overlap rules than a brief damage-over-time effect. Scale consequence with field coverage, source tracking, contact frequency, arena constraints, and the cost of cleansing rather than with theme alone.

designNotes.title: Make ownership and stacking deterministic
designNotes.body: For multiple bosses, summons, hazards, or players, decide whether contributions share one gauge, create separate gauges, or select a dominant source. Resolve simultaneous threshold crossings once, preserve the credited source, and keep co-op UI and rollback from applying duplicate effects.

story.title: Runes stain the sword before they bind its bearer
story.body: Kern's first pulse leaves a few glowing marks on Tavi's gauge, and retreat lets them fade. Returning too soon lets two later pulses complete the rune pattern. Only then do the shards close around Tavi, making accumulation, threshold, and consequence three readable story beats.

adaptation.title: Offer redundant warning and adjustable recovery
adaptation.body: Pair the gauge with shape, icon, sound, caption, and controller feedback at important bands. Allow larger UI, reduced flashes, independent effect audio, and a clear numeric or segmented alternative. Difficulty options may increase decay, reduce buildup, lengthen immunity, or automate cleansing without hiding the underlying rule.

distinction.title: A thresholded secondary state, not ordinary health or a posture break
distinction.body: Health usually changes immediately when damage resolves. A posture gauge commonly rewards sustained player pressure by opening the boss to a finisher. Status buildup instead records exposure on a target and withholds its separate payload until a threshold is crossed; that payload may harm, constrain, transform, or defeat either side.

lensNotes.body: The gauge must distinguish partial exposure, decay, threshold crossing, active effect, and immunity without implying that they are the same state.
Remaining in range can preserve offensive uptime, but it also postpones decay and makes the next contact more likely to cross the threshold.
Leaving the source, guarding a tick, cleansing, or building resistance must change a measurable part of the accumulation rule.
Contact spacing relative to the decay delay determines whether pressure feels like isolated warnings or a deliberate threshold combo.
Cleansing, resistance, immunity, and sources that bypass decay are exceptions that need explicit ownership and visible feedback.

examples.body: The boss's poison breath and summoned Stenchpods turn one shared poison meter into an arena-pressure system. Exposure fills the gauge first; poisoning begins only after it fills, so retreat space and the time between contacts determine whether partial buildup becomes a lasting effect.

The headless phase's scream applies Terror over a broad radial area. The visible meter separates brief exposure from the lethal threshold, letting the sustained field, escape time, and any buildup reduction be tuned independently of the scream's ordinary damage.

Wormface's breath and lingering cloud build Death Blight rather than immediately producing its terminal result. Moving sources and persistent space denial can therefore share one threshold while the full meter remains the single authoritative transition to the effect.
